Reconstructing acoustic structures and their attached components from recorded sounds is a complex problem with many possible solutions. However, for many applications, it's not enough to simply identify the presence of a specific component; rather, it's necessary to determine the precise features of that component from the sound data. This challenge becomes even more difficult when the data contains errors or if the component in question has a complex shape. In this paper, a new approach is presented that uses a hybrid method, combining deep learning and level set techniques, to accurately define the boundaries of acoustic components based on sound patterns, even in the presence of noisy data, and demonstrates this approach's effectiveness on real-world data. This research provides a starting point for more advanced techniques that can handle more intricate shapes and multiple components, as well as exploring the possibilities of reversing the problem to recover missing structural data from sound patterns. This work is relevant to fields such as non-destructive testing and audio-based monitoring of mechanical systems. The associated code can be found at https://github.com/insar-group/ACO. The model was implemented using PyTorch, a deep learning framework, and the level set method was implemented using Python. The code consists of approximately 10 lines of PyTorch code and approximately 50 lines of Python level set code. The algorithm works as follows. First, the sound data is preprocessed using a deep learning-based approach, then a level set method is used to obtain an initial approximation of the structure, from which a finite element method-derived contrast function is computed, which in turn is used to update the level set, until the desired precision is reached. The ESS framework yields an approximate, yet precise, explanation for the light sterile neutrino's tiny mass and the dark matter particle's mass range. The number of chest X-rays being collected is rising exponentially due to COVID-19, leading to a significant challenge of effectively managing and storing them, while ensuring patient safety and adherence to medical regulations. In response to this issue, some hospitals are considering implementing algorithms to anonymize their images. However, developing robust methods to detect image alteration remains crucial, given the tendency for patients to complain about their images being modified. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach that combines a simple technique for blurring images and encourages researchers to focus on more complex methods to detect alterations, as evidenced by a related classification task. This research was conducted during the COVID-19 outbreak when chest X-rays were being modified on a large scale, providing a practical application for any resulting methods. Our findings used 7 datasets, including the COVID-19 category, and our proposed approach has been openly sourced on GitHub. It is also worth noting that our method prioritizes simplicity over complexity, as reflected in our results, which demonstrate that even a straightforward blurring technique can deceive over 80% of deep-learning-based classifiers with confidence. Our research has further implications for securing confidential information on brain and mammography images, which could also be tested against our proposed framework. Given the limited nature of our current dataset, we are confident that a larger, more comprehensive dataset would yield more impressive results. ViDaExpert is an application program for the visual interpretation and analysis of multidimensional data.  It is capable of processing datasets from various sources, including KDD files produced by our earlier ViDa tool.  Once processed, these datasets can be represented in different nonlinear formats, such as multivariate Gaussian distributions, decision trees, neural networks, clustering models, and support vector machines.  These representations can be further examined to identify complex relationships between variables, detect anomalies, and verify the accuracy of models.  ViDaExpert offers a user-friendly graphical interface, allowing experts and novice users to effectively analyze high-dimensional datasets with ease.  This instrument is tailored for use in education, research, and various data analysis applications.  ViDaExpert runs on Windows 95/98/NT platforms and is available for download on the Internet.  A related student tutorial is also provided.  ViDaExpert's source code is intended for advanced users and researchers who wish to customize and extend the instrument's capabilities.  A research grant from the University of Nevada, Las Vegas funded this project.  ViDaExpert was previously known as Visual Data Expert.
